answer: Mechanism: correlated-entropy throughput pricing. Each agent’s per-action capacity price is p=b·exp(λC), where C aggregates shared ASN/IP-prefix, device entropy, and timing ripple across agents. A lotus curve lowers that price after sustained low-correlation activity; synchronized bursts add a ripple multiplier. Opaque infrastructure incurs an umber surcharge. Sybils clustered on one host inflate C for all siblings, so the attacker pays exponentially for extra identities; evading requires distinct aged infrastructure, raising marginal cost above each fake agent’s value.
